evals.prompt: List the currently discovered Vals benchmarks and identify any with unknown score semantics.
evals.expected_output: One compact JSON catalog response listing source-discovered Vals benchmarks, explicit provenance, and warnings for benchmarks whose score type is not safely comparable.
expectations: The response has exactly one compact JSON object on stdout and uses the vals source provenance, source URL, discovered-from URL, fetched_at, parser, parser_version, and source hash when supplied.
Every listed benchmark preserves its explicit release/version, or reports null/missing rather than inventing one.
Every model row preserves model, provider, and variant identity, including explicit null for an absent variant.
Unknown score fields have metric_semantics_status unknown and UNKNOWN_SCORE_SEMANTICS; they are not labeled pass_at_1, accuracy, or another familiar family.
Placeholder values such as 0.0%, N/A, em dash, and empty strings are missing/null with a reason and never ranked as measurements.
The response does not silently use stale data or an older release after a refresh failure; stale data is visible only when explicitly requested.
Unknown catalog and metric fields remain under raw_metadata or raw_fields with original names and values.
A newly present benchmark is listed through dynamic discovery without requiring a current-catalog allow-list or production-code branch.

evals.prompt: Compare three models on Vals’ currently available coding-related benchmarks, preserving benchmark versions, score definitions, cost, latency, and uncertainty.
evals.expected_output: A compact JSON comparison of three full model variants across discovered coding benchmarks, keeping correctness, quality, cost per test, latency per test, uncertainty, benchmark versions, and provenance as separate fields.
expectations: Each row cites the Vals source URL, discovered-from URL, fetched_at, parser/version, and selected benchmark release/version.
Rows retain model, provider, and variant as a complete identity and do not merge variants with the same display model name.
Each score retains its source definition/type; correctness, quality, cost_per_test, latency_per_test, and uncertainty are not collapsed into one incompatible score.
No row uses a placeholder as a published numeric value; missing or unparsed values are explicit with reasons.
The comparison never silently falls back to stale data or substitutes another benchmark/release; any explicit stale mode is labeled in scope/provenance.
New or unknown source fields remain visible under raw_fields without changing known fields.
The benchmark set is discovered from the fixture catalog and can include a new coding benchmark without a benchmark-name branch.
The output separates published values from derived ranking/delta values and includes warnings for non-comparable semantics.

evals.prompt: Find a benchmark that reports code quality separately from correctness and report both without averaging them.
evals.expected_output: A source-backed JSON result with separate correctness and code-quality values, quality scale/evaluator metadata, model variants, benchmark version, and provenance; no composite average.
expectations: Provenance names the official Vals source URL, release/version, fetched_at, extraction method, parser/version, and source paths for both metrics.
Model/provider/variant identity is retained for every correctness and quality observation.
Correctness score semantics and quality score semantics/scales/evaluator are separate and no average or pass_at_1 relabeling is emitted.
A placeholder or absent quality value is null/missing with a reason, never a zero-quality measurement.
The command does not silently substitute stale quality/correctness data or a different benchmark version.
Quality evaluator and any newly supplied metadata remain in raw_fields when not understood.
The benchmark and its quality field are discovered from source records, not from a fixed benchmark allow-list.
Derived recommendations, if requested, label their inputs and never overwrite the two published source values.

evals.prompt: Simulate or use a fixture with a newly added benchmark and prove it is discovered without code changes.
evals.expected_output: A compact fixture-backed catalog and comparison response showing a novel benchmark, its preserved raw metadata, and an unknown-semantics warning without an implementation branch for its name.
expectations: The new benchmark record includes source/discovered-from URLs, fetched_at, source release/version, extraction method, parser/version, and hash provenance.
Any model rows for the new benchmark preserve model/provider/variant identity and do not collide with existing rows.
Its unfamiliar score is marked unknown and excluded from known-family ranking rather than being treated as pass_at_1 or accuracy.
Placeholder/malformed values in the new record remain missing/unparsed and are not used as numeric measurements.
The test uses the explicit fixture snapshot and never silently falls back to a prior catalog or stale artifact.
The new benchmark's display name, URL, and all unknown fields survive under raw_metadata/raw_fields.
Catalog output and catalog-diff report the addition dynamically; no hardcoded benchmark slug or production-code branch is required.
The response contains a structured UNKNOWN_SCORE_SEMANTICS warning explaining why comparison is blocked.

evals.prompt: Report a source drift problem when a benchmark page contains placeholder scores.
evals.expected_output: A diagnostic JSON response identifying placeholder values and their source paths, excluding them from rankings while preserving usable rows and provenance.
expectations: The diagnostic cites the official/fixture source URL, resolved release/version, fetched_at, extraction method, parser/version, and affected source paths.
Usable rows retain model/provider/variant identity; unusable rows remain inspectable with explicit identity when available.
0.0%, N/A, em dash, and empty placeholders produce PLACEHOLDER_VALUE/missing diagnostics and are never ranked as real scores.
The benchmark score definition remains distinct from quality/cost/latency and no placeholder becomes pass_at_1 or accuracy.
A refresh failure does not silently produce an older-release result; explicit stale mode is labeled and otherwise returns an error.
Unknown placeholder-related fields and original raw values remain under raw_fields/raw_metadata.
Partial usable output is ok:true only with separated warnings; an entirely unusable page is ok:false rather than an empty success.
The CLI emits one compact JSON object on stdout and keeps operational diagnostics on stderr without secrets.
